<p>Refuse &amp; recycling</p><p>Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, notwithstanding the details</p><p>as shown on the approved drawings, precise details of the proposed refuse and recycling</p><p>storage capacity shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning</p><p>Authority. The development shall thereafter be carried out in strict accordance with the</p><p>approved details and the area shall remain free from obstruction other than for its approved</p><p>use.</p><p>REASON: To ensure adequate provision for refuse and recycling is provided which would</p><p>safeguard the amenity of the area and not compromise pedestrian safety, in accordance with</p><p>Local Plan policy LP57.</p>

<p>Secured by Design</p><p>Prior to occupation, the development shall achieve a Certificate of Compliance to the relevant</p><p>Secure by Design Guide(s) with the Metropolitan Police. The approved details submitted to</p><p>the Metropolitan Police and the awarded Certificate must then be submitted to and approved</p><p>in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to occupation.</p><p>The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter</p><p>shall be fully retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the building functions securely, in a manner consistent with the</p><p>principles of ‘Secured by Design’,, in accordance with London Plan policy D11 and Local</p><p>Plan policy LP1.</p>

<p>Survey for nesting birds</p><p>Prior to any demolition or site clearance works, an updated bat and bird survey must be</p><p>undertaken to establish the likely presence of a bat roost or bird nest. Furthermore, a</p><p>pre-works ecological check for nesting birds must be carried out by a suitably qualified</p><p>ecologist during nesting season (March - August) before any demolition or site clearance</p><p>commences. The findings and recommendations of both surveys, including any necessary</p><p>mitigation or avoidance measures, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local</p><p>Planning Authority. Works shall proceed strictly in accordance with the approved</p><p>recommendations.</p><p>REASON: To support and protect bird and bat populations in Hackney and preserve</p><p>endangered biodiversity, in line with the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.</p>

<p>Demolition &amp; Construction Logistics Management Plan</p><p>Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved, a Demolition and Construction</p><p>Management Plan shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning</p><p>authority. The Plan shall be submitted in accordance with Hackney Council’s Code of</p><p>Construction Practice and the Mayor of London's Control of Dust and Emissions during</p><p>Construction and Demolition SPG, and other relevant guidance relating to dust and air</p><p>quality. The development shall be implemented in accordance with details and measures</p><p>approved in the Plan, covering the matters set out below, and shall be maintained throughout</p><p>the entire construction period:</p><p>a) Demolition and construction method statement, covering all phases of the development, to</p><p>include the result of the construction dust risk assessment and details of noise control</p><p>measures;</p><p>b) Site waste management plan setting out how resources will be managed and waste</p><p>controlled at all stages of the project, including, but not limited to, details of dust mitigation</p><p>measures to deal with construction waste during site clearance, demolition and</p><p>construction works (including any breaking or crushing of concrete), and details of</p><p>measures to be employed to mitigate noise and vibration demonstrating best practical</p><p>means;</p><p>c) An air quality and dust management plan, to include details of measures to control and</p><p>mitigate emissions of dust from site clearance, demolition and construction activity,</p><p>following best practice guidance, including installation of noise, vibration and dust (NVD)</p><p>monitoring systems and appropriate locations around the site;</p><p>d) A demolition and construction traffic management plan to include the following: the</p><p>construction programme/timescales, details of locations where deliveries will be</p><p>undertaken, the size and number/frequency of vehicles expected to access the site per</p><p>day, pedestrian and vehicular access arrangements (including turning arrangements if</p><p>necessary), construction traffic route and trip generation, any temporary road/footway</p><p>closures during the construction period, details of parking suspensions (if required) and</p><p>the duration of works;</p><p>e) The operation of site equipment generating noise and other nuisance causing activities,</p><p>audible beyond the site boundary, shall only be carried out between the hours of</p><p>08:00-18:00 Mondays to Fridays, 08:00-13:00 Saturdays, and at no time on Sundays or</p><p>bank holidays. The best practical means available, in accordance with British Standard</p><p>Code of Practice BS5228-1:2009 shall be employed at all times to minimise emission of</p><p>noise and vibration.</p><p>f) Details of how the site will comply with the relevant Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM)</p><p>regulations</p><p>The Demolition and Construction Management Plan shall set out how the following will be</p><p>adhered to:</p><p>● A Notice Board shall be erected externally to have contact details for the Site and</p><p>Regional Office posted. The contact details should be sufficient for Planning</p><p>Enforcement and Environmental Health to be able to contact an appropriate person in</p><p>event of complaints. The main contractor is requested to submit contact details to the</p><p>planning authority and to display them on the site board at the site entrance:</p><p>● Details of at Least two relevant named individuals including their job role (one of whom</p><p>should ideally be an off-site main office contact);</p><p>● Postal addresses;</p><p>● E-mail details; and,</p><p>● Mobile details with a robust arrangement for out of hours’ complaints</p><p>REASON: To protect air quality and human health by minimising emissions during</p><p>construction, to minimise nuisance caused by dust, noise and vibration, to avoid hazard and</p><p>obstruction being caused to users of the public highway and in the interest of public safety</p><p>and amenity,in accordance with with Local Plan policy LP58 and London Plan Policy SI 1,</p>

<p>Energy Statement</p><p>Prior to above ground works (except demolition), a revised Energy Statement shall be</p><p>submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority, providing full details to</p><p>demonstrate at least the following standards and key metrics have been achieved or</p><p>improved upon as set out in the hereby approved Energy Statement (Revision P02 by XCO2</p><p>dated April 2025):</p><p>a) Minimum carbon savings of 24.4 % / 3.96 tonnes CO2e against Part L 2021 through fabric</p><p>efficiency (Be Lean)</p><p>b) Minimum overall carbon savings of 81.0% / 13.16 tonnes CO2e Part L 2021</p><p>c) Maximum U-values (W/m2K): walls 0.15; floor 0.10; roof 0.10; windows 1.20; doors 1.00</p><p>unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority</p><p>d) Maximum G-values for windows and doors of 0.5 unless otherwise agreed in writing with</p><p>the Local Planning Authority</p><p>e) Maximum Air permeability of 2m3</p><p>/m2</p><p>.h at 50Pa unless otherwise agreed in writing with the</p><p>Local Planning Authority</p><p>f) Maximum Space Heating demand of 15kWh/sqm/yr using a predictive modelling</p><p>calculation methodology such as PHPP, TM54 or equivalent - the applicant will be expected</p><p>to demonstrate and quantify how further design works have been carried out to seek to</p><p>achieve the planning application target of 10.3kWh/sqm/yr unless otherwise agreed in writing</p><p>with the Local Planning Authority</p><p>g) Maximum Energy Use Intensity of 35 kWh/sqm/yr using a predictive modelling calculation</p><p>methodology PHPP, TM54 or equivalent - the applicant will be expected to demonstrate and</p><p>quantify how further design works have been carried out to seek to achieve the design target</p><p>of 59.9 unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority - the applicant</p><p>will be expected to benchmark the results against the UK Net Zero Carbon Building Standard</p><p>relevant data sets</p><p>h) A third party review report of the as-design predictive modelling calculations</p><p>i) Updated GLA Carbon Emission Reporting Spreadsheet</p><p>The operational carbon emissions must be calculated using the appropriate methodology for</p><p>all the identified units - in the exceptional circumstances that all units can not be reasonably</p><p>assessed, a representative sample must be used and include:</p><p>- at least one unit for each identified flat type/area type, and</p><p>- any unit subject to the following criteria: units (a) with large glazing areas, (b) on the</p><p>topmost floor, (c) having limited shading, (d) having large, sun-facing windows, (e) having a</p><p>single aspect, or (c) having limited opening windows</p><p>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, air permeability certificates</p><p>prepared by a suitable contractor must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local</p><p>Planning Authority confirming the approved figures have been achieved or improved upon</p><p>REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net</p><p>zero development and construction, in accordance with LP54, LP55 and LP56 of the</p><p>Hackney Local Plan, SI2, SI3, SI4 and SI7 of the London Plan, and Section 14 of the</p><p>National Planning Policy Framework</p>

<p>Time limit</p><p>The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years</p><p>beginning with the date of this permission.</p><p>REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990</p><p>(as amended).</p>

<p>Post-installation noise assessment</p><p>The use hereby permitted, or the operation of any building services plant, shall not</p><p>commence until a post-installation noise assessment has been carried out to confirm</p><p>compliance with the noise criteria. The scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the</p><p>approved details and attenuation measures, and they shall be permanently retained and</p><p>maintained in working order for the duration of the use and their operation.</p><p>REASON: To protect the amenities of adjoining occupiers and the surrounding area, in</p><p>accordance with Local Plan policy LP2.</p>

<p>Overheating</p><p>a) Prior to the commencement of above ground works (except demolition), a dynamic</p><p>overheating risk assessment must be submitted to and approved by the Local Authority,</p><p>assessing all units and following the CIBSE TM52 (non residential) &amp; TM59 (residential)</p><p>methodology.</p><p>The assessment must include design specific details of how each steps of the Cooling</p><p>Hierarchy has been implemented, for reference these are:</p><p>- Step 1: Reduce the amount of heat entering a building in summer through orientation,</p><p>shading, albedo, fenestration, insulation and green roofs and walls</p><p>- Step 2: Minimise internal heat generation through energy efficient design</p><p>- Step 3: Manage the heat within the building through exposed internal thermal mass and</p><p>high ceilings</p><p>- Step 4: Passive ventilation</p><p>- Step 5: Mechanical ventilation</p><p>- Step 6:Active cooling systems</p><p>All report results of the dynamic modelling in line with the CIBSE TM52 and TM59</p><p>compliance criteria must clearly set out the pass rate (%) of each of the Cooling Hierarchy</p><p>steps, using baseline scenario and additional modelled scenario to test all mitigations</p><p>(passive first, active as last resort) measures required until all units pass the overheating risk</p><p>assessment - as follows:</p><p>- Step 1 mitigation measures description leading to pass rate percentage</p><p>- Step 2 mitigation measures description leading to pass rate percentage</p><p>All units must be assessed against weather files CIBSE TM49 DSY1, DSY2 &amp; DSY3, results</p><p>should demonstrate a 100% pass rate for all units shown under weather file DSY1 - in the</p><p>exceptional circumstances that all units can not be reasonably assessed, a representative</p><p>sample must be used and include:</p><p>1. at least one unit for each identified flat type/area type, and</p><p>2. any unit subject to the following criteria: units (a) with large glazing areas, (b) on the</p><p>topmost floor, (c) having limited shading, (d) having large, sun-facing windows, (e) having</p><p>a single aspect, or (c) having limited opening windows</p><p>The applicant should provide supporting evidence such as scope drawings highlighting what</p><p>unit/area have been included in the modelling.</p><p>If 100% pass rate is not achieved under weather files DSY2 &amp; 3, a retrofit plan must be</p><p>submitted to and approved by the Local Authority detailing how further mitigation measures</p><p>can be installed and who will be responsible to manage future overheating risk for 100% of</p><p>units to pass under both weather files DSY2 and DSY3.</p><p>Where any additional remedial mitigation measures are required, the product specifications</p><p>and details must be provided.</p><p>b) Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, a final “as-built” overheating</p><p>risk assessment shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority,</p><p>assessing all units and following the CIBSE TM52 (non residential) &amp; TM59 (residential)</p><p>methodology, confirming % pass rates for each TM49 weather file have or improved upon</p><p>pre-commencement figures following the prospective retrofit measures.</p><p>REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net</p><p>zero development and construction, in accordance with Local Plan policies LP54 and LP55;</p><p>London Plan policies SI 2 and SI 4; and NPPF section 14.</p>

<p>External materials</p><p>Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition) scaled detailed</p><p>drawings, product references and images of all externally facing construction materials,</p><p>boundary treatments and ground surfaces must be submitted to, and approved in writing by</p><p>the Local Planning Authority (LPA). Samples of the proposed materials must also be made</p><p>available on site for potential inspection and retrained for the duration of the works. The</p><p>proposal must be implemented and maintained thereafter in perpetuity in accordance with</p><p>the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the LPA.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and does</p><p>not detract from the character of the area, in accordance with Local Plan policies PP1, LP1</p><p>and LP3 and London Plan policy D4.</p>

<p>Privacy of northernmost ground floor flat</p><p>The west-facing window serving the northernmost ground floor flat must be obscurely glazed</p><p>and non-opening below a height of 1.7m from the floor finish level of the room it serves.</p><p>REASON: To maintain privacy of future occupiers, in accordance with Local Plan policy LP2.</p>

<p>Privacy of upper floor flats with east-facing balconies</p><p>Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition) details of privacy</p><p>screening between the upper floor private balconies on the east elevation must be submitted</p><p>to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA). Samples of the proposed</p><p>materials must also be made available on site for potential inspection and retrained for the</p><p>duration of the works. The proposal must be implemented and maintained thereafter in</p><p>perpetuity in accordance with the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the</p><p>LPA.</p><p>REASON: To maintain privacy of future occupiers, in accordance with Local Plan policy LP2.</p>

<p>Accessible dwellings</p><p>At least 10% units within the development hereby approved must be completed in</p><p>compliance with Building Regulations Optional Requirement Part M4(3) 'wheelchair user</p><p>dwellings' (or any subsequent replacement) prior to first occupation and shall be retained as</p><p>thereafter for the lifetime of the development. The remaining dwellings must be built and</p><p>maintained to a minimum of M4(2) standard.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the development is adequately accessible for all occupiers, in</p><p>accordance with London Plan policy D7.</p>

<p>Parking Design and Management Plan (PDMP)</p><p>Prior to first occupation, details of the PDMP shall be submitted to and approved in writing by</p><p>the Local Planning Authority (LPA).</p><p>The PDMP shall:</p><p>a) Demonstrate safe design of the agreed number of on-street car parking spaces and</p><p>access for pedestrians and cyclists and minimisation of conflict between use groups; and</p><p>b) Appropriate provision of Blue Badge parking and electric vehicle charging points; and</p><p>include details of how additional blue badge car parking could be provided in future; and</p><p>c) Permanent Mechanisms for prevention of non-car parking areas to be controlled for that</p><p>purpose; and</p><p>d) Ensure that use of car parking for the relevant is actively controlled through measures to</p><p>enforce the car parking arrangements for the relevant block</p><p>The approved PDMP must be implemented in full prior to occupation of the development,</p><p>and thereafter retained for lifetime of the development, unless otherwise agreed in writing by</p><p>the LPA.</p><p>REASON: In the interests of highway safety and the amenity of neighbouring occupiers, and</p><p>in accordance with Local Plan policies LP41, LP42, LP44 and LP45 and London Plan policy</p><p>T6.1.</p>

<p>Cycle parking</p><p>Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition) scaled drawings of</p><p>the proposed cycle stores (including living roofs) and any external stands must be submitted</p><p>to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p>The details must demonstrate a policy compliant number of spaces and a design that is safe,</p><p>secure and accessible.</p><p>REASON: To ensure adequate provision for the safe and secure storage of bicycles, to</p><p>promote sustainable modes of transport, in accordance with Local Plan policy LP42.</p>

<p>Archaeology</p><p>No demolition or development shall take place until a stage 1 written scheme of investigation</p><p>(WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land</p><p>that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in</p><p>accordance with the agreed WSI, and the programme and methodology of site evaluation</p><p>and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works.</p><p>If heritage assets of archaeological interest are identified by stage 1 then for those parts of</p><p>the site which have archaeological interest a stage 2 WSI shall be submitted to and approved</p><p>by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the stage 2 WSI, no</p><p>demolition/development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed stage 2</p><p>WSI which shall include:</p><p>A. The statement of significance and research objectives, the programme and methodology</p><p>of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or</p><p>organisation to undertake the agreed works.</p><p>B. Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefits.</p><p>C. The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication &amp;</p><p>dissemination and deposition of resulting material. This part of the condition shall not be</p><p>discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set</p><p>out in the stage 2 WSI.</p><p>REASON: This pre-commencement condition is necessary to safeguard archaeological</p><p>interest on this site. Approval of the SS! Before works begin on site provides clarity on what</p><p>investigations are required, and their timing in relation to the development programme, in</p><p>accordance with NPPF paragraph 218.</p>

<p>Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM)</p><p>All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37 kW and up to and including 560</p><p>kW used during the course of site preparation, demolition and construction phases must</p><p>comply with the emissions standards of the Mayor of London's NRMM Low Emission Zone.</p><p>Unless in compliance with the NRMM Low Emission Zone standards, no NRMM must be</p><p>on-site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local</p><p>planning authority. The applicant shall keep an up-to-date register of all NRMM used during</p><p>site preparation, demolition and construction phases on the online register at</p><p>https://www.london.gov.uk/programmes-and-strategies/environment-and-climate-change/poll</p><p>ution-and-air-quality/nrmm.</p><p>REASON: To ensure emissions from the site during the construction phase are acceptable</p><p>with regard to public health and amenity, in accordance with London Plan Policy SI 1.</p>

<p>Land contamination</p><p>Prior to commencing the works, for each section of the development or stage in the</p><p>development - as may be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA) - a scheme</p><p>including the following components to address the risks associated with site contamination</p><p>shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by the LPA.</p><p>a) A generic and detailed quantitative risk assessment that identifies the risk to all receptors</p><p>potentially affected, including those off site;</p><p>b) In the event that remediation measures are deemed necessary following the results of (a),</p><p>an options appraisal identifying feasible remediation options, detailing evaluation of options,</p><p>and selecting the most appropriate remediation option(s);</p><p>c) A remediation strategy focused on the remediation option(s) selected in (b) setting site</p><p>specific monitoring objectives and criteria, providing details of monitoring and maintenance,</p><p>and containing full details of the remediation measures required, and how they are to be</p><p>undertaken.</p><p>d) A verification plan explaining how the effectiveness of the remediation works set out in ©</p><p>will be measured, and how data will be collected and assessed to demonstrate that the</p><p>remediation objectives and criteria will be met.</p><p>e) A verification report demonstrating that remediation objectives and criteria identified in (d)</p><p>have been met, assessing the remediation performance, and creating a final record of the</p><p>land quality whilst providing a plan for long term monitoring and maintenance (if required).</p><p>Any investigation and risk assessment must be undertaken in strict accordance with the</p><p>requirements of the Environment Agency’s Land Contamination Risk Management (LCRM).</p><p>If additional significant contamination is found at any time when carrying out the approved</p><p>development, it must immediately be reported in writing to the LPA.</p><p>For the avoidance of doubt, this condition can be discharged on a section by section basis.</p><p>REASON: To protect human health and the environment by ensuring no harm is caused by</p><p>land contamination, in accordance with Local Plan policy LP58 and the Hackney</p><p>contaminated land strategy 2022/2030</p>

<p>Post installation test</p><p>A post installation test shall be carried out prior to occupation to demonstrate that all</p><p>residential premises designed in accordance with “BS8233:2014 - Guidance on Sound</p><p>Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings” achieving the required internal noise levels</p><p>cited in Table 2 of the report, Appendixes, below have been met and the results submitted to</p><p>the Local Planning Authority for approval.</p><p>Activity/Location/0700-2300 hours/2300-0700 hours</p><p>Resting/Living room/35dBLaeq16h/-</p><p>Dining/Dining room/40dBLaeq16h/-</p><p>Sleeping or resting/35dBLaeq16h/30dBLaeq16h</p><p>REASON: To obtain required sound insulation and prevent noise nuisance, in accordance</p><p>with Local Plan policy LP2.</p>

<p>Sound insulation in and between dwellings</p><p>Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition), a scheme of</p><p>sound insulation measures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Council, of</p><p>an enhanced sound insulation value DnT,w [and L’nT,w] of at least 5dB above the standards</p><p>of Building Regulations Approved Document E ‘Resistance to the passage of sound’ for the</p><p>floor/ceiling/wall structures separating different types of rooms/ uses in adjoining dwellings,</p><p>namely [eg. living room and kitchen above bedroom of separate dwelling]. Approved details</p><p>shall be implemented prior to occupation of the development and thereafter be permanently</p><p>retained.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the amenity of occupiers of the development site is not adversely</p><p>affected by noise, in accordance with Local Plan policy LP2.</p>

<p>Plant/machinery noise</p><p>Any new plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to</p><p>prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise</p><p>level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise</p><p>level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise</p><p>sensitive premises. An assessment of the expected noise levels shall be carried out by a</p><p>suitably qualified (IOA accredited) and experienced acoustic consultant, in accordance with</p><p>BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 ‘Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound,’</p><p>and any mitigation measures necessary to achieve the above required noise levels shall be</p><p>submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval.</p><p>The plant shall thereafter be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved</p><p>details.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the amenity of occupiers of the development site and neighbouring</p><p>amenity is not adversely affected by noise, in accordance with Local Plan policy LP2.</p>

<p>Piling method statement</p><p>No piling shall take place until a piling method statement (detailing the depth and type of</p><p>piling to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling will be carried out,</p><p>including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface</p><p>sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for the works) and piling layout plan including all</p><p>Thames Water wastewater assets, the local topography and clearance between the face of</p><p>the pile to the face of a pipe has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local</p><p>planning authority in consultation with Thames Water.</p><p>Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms of the approved piling method</p><p>statement and piling layout plan.</p><p>REASON: The proposed works will be in close proximity to underground sewerage utility</p><p>infrastructure. Piling has the potential to significantly impact / cause failure of local</p><p>underground sewerage utility infrastructure.</p>

<p>Surface water drainage</p><p>a) No development shall commence, other than works of demolition until full detailed</p><p>specification of the sustainable drainage system supported by appropriate calculations,</p><p>construction details, drainage layout and a site-specific management and maintenance plan</p><p>of the sustainable drainage system has been provided. Details shall include but not limited to</p><p>the proposed blue-green roofs with shallow attenuation crates, permeable paving,</p><p>bio-retention features (rain gardens and tree pits), underground geocellular attenuation tank</p><p>and the flow control system, which shall be submitted and approved by the Local Planning</p><p>Authority (LPA) in consultation with the LLFA. A peak discharge rate must also be specified</p><p>for all return periods up to the 1 in 100 year storm events, plus an allowance for climate</p><p>change.</p><p>b) Evidence (including as-built drawings, photographs, post construction surveys) and a final</p><p>completion statement signed off by a qualified drainage engineer should be submitted and</p><p>approved by the LPA showing that the sustainable drainage system has been constructed as</p><p>per the approved designs and in accordance with best practice.</p><p>c) A scheme for the provision and implementation of flood resilient and resistant construction</p><p>details and measures for the site against surface water flood risk shall be submitted to and</p><p>agreed in writing with the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA, prior to the construction of the</p><p>measures. The scheme shall confirm that the finished floor level (FFL) of all ground-floor</p><p>areas, and that safe access and egress are maintained. The approved scheme shall be</p><p>implemented in its entirety before the site is occupied and shall be constructed and</p><p>completed in accordance with the details approved under this condition and in line with BS</p><p>8582:2013 code of practice for "surface water management for development sites".</p><p>For the avoidance of doubt, this condition can be discharged on a section by section basis.</p><p>REASON: In the interest of flood resilience against surface water flood risk, in accordance</p><p>with London Plan policy SI 12 and Local Plan policy LP53.</p>

<p>Tree Protection</p><p>Tree protection for trees marked T1 (sweet gum) and T2 (London plane) in 6.6 Trees section</p><p>of the Design and Access statement included with this application, on adjacent land shall be</p><p>undertaken in accordance with BS5837:2012 (Trees in relation to construction -</p><p>Recommendations) The protective fencing will be 2.4m high and conform to Figure 2 of</p><p>BS5837:2012 i.e. a scaffold framework comprising a vertical and horizontal framework, well</p><p>braced to resist impacts, with vertical tubes spaced at a maximum interval of 3m. On to this</p><p>weldmesh panels should be securely fixed with wire or scaffold clamps, unless first approved</p><p>in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p>REASON: To accord with the requirements of Section 197(a) of the Town and Country</p><p>Planning Act 1990 and to provide reasonable environmental standards in the interests of the</p><p>appearance of the site and area.</p>

<p>No service runs within Root Protection Areas</p><p>All new underground utility apparatus, including drainage, shall be routed and installed</p><p>outside the Root Protection Area(s) (RPAs) shown on the approved drawings. Should it not</p><p>be feasible to route new underground utility apparatus outside the RPAs of retained trees,</p><p>trenchless insertion methods (as detailed in BS 5837:2012, Table 3) shall be employed for</p><p>their installation within the RPAs, with entry and retrieval pits sited outside the RPAs. No</p><p>other new underground utilities shall be installed within the RPAs of retained trees without</p><p>prior written consent from the Local Planning Authority. Any such works, if permitted, shall be</p><p>carried out in strict accordance with the principles of BS 5837:2012 "Trees in relation to</p><p>design, demolition and construction – Recommendations" and the National Joint Utilities</p><p>Group Guidelines for the planning, installation and maintenance of utility apparatus in</p><p>proximity to trees, Volume 4, Issue 2 (2007) (or any standard that reproduces or replaces this</p><p>standard).</p><p>REASON: To safeguard existing tree(s) in the interests of visual amenity and long-term tree</p><p>health, having regard to Local Plan policy LP51. Prior approval is required to ensure that</p><p>important trees are not permanently damaged or lost due to root disturbance or changes in</p><p>soil hydrology.</p>

<p>Landscaping plan</p><p>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, detailed drawings and plans for</p><p>the soft landscaping scheme must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local</p><p>Planning Authority.</p><p>The details must include:</p><p>- A tree planting plan consisting of a diverse mix of species that follows as a minimum, the</p><p>10-20-30% rule (species/genus/family diversity), including both those adapted to changing</p><p>climatic conditions and native species, which are known to have value to wildlife;</p><p>- Soil volumes for proposed tree planting;</p><p>- Projected mature height and crown spread of proposed new trees;</p><p>- Tree pit specifications and planter specifications for above ground tree planting;</p><p>- Methods of tree support - e.g. staking or underground guying and protection - e.g. tree</p><p>guards, grilles etc;</p><p>- A varied plant structure, incorporating flowering plants, evergreen species, and shrubs to</p><p>enhance habitat diversity;</p><p>- A diverse distribution of plant species to avoid block planting;</p><p>- A detailed tree planting plan including details of trees and shrubs showing species, size at</p><p>planting, type of stock, age of tree at planting, numbers of trees and shrubs to be</p><p>included;</p><p>- Areas to be grass seeded or turfed;</p><p>All landscaping in accordance with the scheme, when approved, shall be carried out within a</p><p>period of twelve months from the date on which the development of the site commences or</p><p>shall be carried out in the first planting (and seeding) season following completion of the</p><p>development, and shall be maintained to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority for a</p><p>period of ten years, such maintenance to include the replacement of any trees or plants that</p><p>die, or are severely damaged, seriously diseased, or removed.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the site protects and enhances biodiversity, in accordance with</p><p>Local Plan policies LP47 and LP51 and Section 15 of the National Planning Policy</p><p>Framework.</p>

<p>External Lighting Scheme</p><p>Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition), an External</p><p>Lighting Scheme must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning</p><p>Authority. The scheme must be designed and implemented in accordance with the Bat</p><p>Conservation Trust guidelines and must be sensitive to wildlife. The lighting design should</p><p>ensure that:</p><p>- Harsh lighting is minimised to avoid making habitats (including the green roofs)</p><p>unfavourable to local species, particularly bats and other nocturnal wildlife. The use of</p><p>low-intensity lighting is prioritised, ensuring that any light sources do not directly illuminate</p><p>bat roosts, foraging areas, or flight paths.</p><p>- All lighting fixtures are shielded or directed to limit light pollution and to maintain dark</p><p>corridors that are critical for bat and wildlife movement.</p><p>- LED luminaries should be used for their sharp cut off and dimming capacity. Lighting must</p><p>have no upward spill, favour warm white luminaires, avoid UV light and blue content.</p><p>Security lamps should be motion triggered.</p><p>REASON: To protect local wildlife, particularly bats, from the negative impacts of artificial</p><p>lighting, and to ensure compliance with the Bat Conservation Trust guidelines in accordance</p><p>with relevant environmental and ecological policies.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition), a detailed UGF</p><p>plan must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority,</p><p>demonstrating how the development on the application site will achieve a minimum UGF</p><p>score of 0.4 (unless robust details are submitted to demonstrate why this is not</p><p>achievable) . The submission must include a clearly colour-coded plan identifying all</p><p>surface cover types within the development. A completed UGF calculation table must be</p><p>provided, detailing each surface cover type with its corresponding UGF value, the total area</p><p>of each surface type, the weighted score for each feature, and the cumulative total UGF</p><p>score for the site. The planting must be implemented in accordance with the details hereby</p><p>approved, which must be implemented prior to first occupation of the development, and the</p><p>urban greening measures and soft landscaping must be maintained thereafter for the</p><p>lifetime of the development.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the development incorporates appropriate urban greening</p><p>measures to enhance biodiversity, mitigate urban heat effects and contribute to</p><p>environmental sustainability, in accordance with Local Plan policy LP48 and the London</p><p>Plan policy G5.”</p>

<p>Bird &amp; Bat boxes</p><p>Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, details and full</p><p>specifications of 2 swift bricks/boxes and/or bird boxes, and 2 bat boxes, must be submitted</p><p>to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details must include:</p><p>- A minimum of X2 swift bricks (same requirements for swift box) incorporated into the</p><p>design of the development. They should be installed in groups of at least 2, and placed at</p><p>or close to eaves level of the development hereby approved. They should be placed at</p><p>least 5m above the ground with a 5m unobstructed flight path, both below and in front of</p><p>the swift brick.</p><p>- The swift brick should be located facing north, east, or north east (direct sunlight should</p><p>be avoided) and should not be placed immediately above doors or windows. Where</p><p>possible, swift bricks should be set flush into the external wall to match adjacent</p><p>brickwork.</p><p>- And/or X2 bird boxes incorporated into the design of the development, with a variety of</p><p>box types (including different sized entrance holes) to provide habitat for diverse bird</p><p>species. The boxes should be installed at or close to the eaves level of the development</p><p>hereby approved. The boxes should be between 3 and 5 metres from the ground, and</p><p>there should be a clear flight path without any obstructions below and directly in front of</p><p>the box. The boxes should be facing north, east or north east (direct sunlight should be</p><p>avoided), and should not be placed immediately above doors or windows. Boxes located</p><p>in the same area should not be placed too close together.</p><p>REASON: To promote biodiversity on site, in accordance with Local Plan policy LP46.</p>

<p>Biosolar Gree roof detail</p><p>Prior to commencement of above ground works (except demolition), full details and</p><p>specifications of the biosolar roof(s) must be submitted to and approved in writing by the</p><p>Local Planning Authority (LPA). Green roofs shall be planted with flowering species that</p><p>provide amenity and biodiversity value at different times of the year. The submission shall</p><p>include the following</p><p>● Detailed drawings of a roof plan identifying where the green roofs will be located and the</p><p>measurement of their coverage; this should include other structures on the roof including</p><p>location of PV panels, roof lights and access points where applicable, and their</p><p>relationship with the green roof;</p><p>● The design of the biosolar roof should be in line with GRO’s code of best practice;</p><p>● Section drawings demonstrating a minimum substrate depth of no less than 80mm for a</p><p>sedum roof, 100mm for extensive living roofs (100mm - 150mm for wildflower species);</p><p>and no less than 250mm for intensive living roofs, 400mm for medium shrubs.</p><p>● Details of the proposed type of invertebrate habitat with a minimum of one feature per</p><p>30m2; which could include areas of bare, unplanted substrates, log piles, boulder or</p><p>stone piles, sand piles;</p><p>● Details of the drainage system for the roof;</p><p>● Details of the planting mix;</p><p>● Including a minimum of 9+ species for sedum roof</p><p>● Including a minimum of 16+ species for wildflower/extensive roof</p><p>● All roofs to be sown with a wide mix of species (standard is 15+ species), the roof should</p><p>not rely on one species of plant life</p><p>● Management and maintenance plan, including access arrangements, irrigation, and</p><p>general maintenance actions of biosolar roof;</p><p>● For biosolar roofs, details of how the roof's design meets fire and building safety</p><p>requirements.</p><p>Within 1 month of the first occupation of the development, evidence must be submitted to</p><p>and approved by the LPA that the green roof(s) has been delivered in line with the approved</p><p>details unless otherwise agreed in writing. The green roof shall be retained thereafter for the</p><p>lifetime of the development in accordance with the approved management and maintenance</p><p>plan.</p><p>REASON: To promote biodiversity on site through green roofs, in accordance with HLocal</p><p>Plan policy LP46.</p>

<p>Air Source Heat Pump</p><p>Prior to above ground works (excluding demolition) full details of the communal heat pump</p><p>based heating system specification and supporting drawings shall be submitted to and</p><p>approved by the Local Authority. This shall demonstrate at least the following standards been</p><p>achieved or further optimised as set out in the hereby approved Sustainability &amp; Energy</p><p>Statement (Revision P02 by XCO2 dated April 2025) and relevant supporting documents:</p><p>1. Minimum Heat pump Coefficient of Performance of 3.78 for the domestic hot water supply</p><p>/ heating supply to provide 100% of the heating and hot water demand.</p><p>2. Details of location of the condenser units from the heat pump systems and noise solutions</p><p>to mitigate impact for nearby sensitive receptors;</p><p>3. Details of refrigerants that are required confirming a Low or Zero Global Warming</p><p>Potential (GWP) and Zero Ozone Depleting Potential (ODP)</p><p>The heat pump thereby approved shall be installed prior to occupation of the development</p><p>hereby approved.</p><p>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, full details including as built</p><p>heating system (or any other related fixed plant adopted) specification and supporting</p><p>drawings and installation certificates by an MCS registered installer must be submitted to and</p><p>approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority confirming the system performance has</p><p>been achieved or improved upon the pre-commencement figures,</p><p>Where compliance is not met, a remedial plan and associated cost plan must be prepared</p><p>and submitted to the Local Authority for approval detailing the necessary measures to meet</p><p>the required level of performance. Shortfalls may attract an additional financial contribution to</p><p>the carbon offset fund.</p><p>REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net</p><p>zero development and construction, in accordance with LP55 and LP56 of the Hackney Local</p><p>Plan, SI2 and SI3 of the London Plan, and Section 14 of the National Planning Policy</p><p>Framework</p>

<p>Photovoltaics (PV)</p><p>Prior to installation of the photovoltaic panel array, full details including PV panels system</p><p>(and any other related fixed plant adopted) specification, operation and maintenance plan,</p><p>fire safety risk assessment and supporting drawings must be submitted to and approved by</p><p>the Local authority to demonstrate that the consented standards have been achieved or</p><p>improved upon as set out in the hereby approved Sustainability &amp; Energy Statement</p><p>(Revision P02 by XCO2 dated April 2025)</p><p>a) Solar PV panels annual electricity peak generation of 8.35 kWp</p><p>b) Horizontally mounted rooftop PV panel array of 41 m2</p><p>c) Detailed roof plan (1:50) showing PV array, maintenance and access paths, other plants</p><p>and services, landscaping including fire breaks where applicable</p><p>d) Detailed Operation &amp; Maintenance manual including fire risk assessment where applicable</p><p>the development hereby approved shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with</p><p>the details thereby approved.</p><p>Where compliance is not met, a remedial plan and associated cost plan must be prepared</p><p>and submitted to the Local Authority for approval detailing the necessary measures to meet</p><p>or improve upon the ‘as designed’ performance. Shortfalls may attract an additional financial</p><p>contribution to the carbon offset fund.</p><p>REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net</p><p>zero development and construction, in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan, SI2</p><p>of the London Plan, and Section 14 of the National Planning Policy Framework.</p>

<p>Mechanical Ventilation with Heat Recovery (MVHR)</p><p>Prior to above ground works (except demolition), full details including ventilation system (or</p><p>any other related fixed plant adopted) specification and supporting drawings must be</p><p>submitted to and approved by the Local Authority to demonstrate at least the following</p><p>standards been achieved or improved upon as set out in the hereby approved Sustainability</p><p>&amp; Energy Statement (Revision P02 by XCO2 dated April 2025):</p><p>a) Minimum MVRH efficiency of 90.00% unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local</p><p>Planning Authority</p><p>b) Details of summer by pass where applicable including provision and location across the</p><p>development</p><p>The MVHR thereby approved shall be installed prior to occupation of the development</p><p>hereby approved.</p><p>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, full details including as built</p><p>ventilation system (or any other related fixed plant adopted) specification and supporting</p><p>drawings and installation certificates by a suitable contractor must be submitted to and</p><p>approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority confirming the ventilation system has</p><p>achieved or improved upon the pre-commencement figures.</p><p>Where compliance is not met, a remedial plan and associated cost plan must be prepared</p><p>and submitted to the Local Authority for approval detailing the necessary measures to meet</p><p>the required level of performance. Shortfalls may attract an additional financial contribution to</p><p>the carbon offset fund.</p><p>REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net</p><p>zero development and construction, in accordance with LP54 and LP55 of the Hackney Local</p><p>Plan, SI2 and SI4 of the London Plan, and Section 14 of the National Planning Policy</p><p>Framework</p>

<p>Site Waste Management Plan (SWMP)</p><p>Notwithstanding details in the submitted draft SWMP, prior to the commencement of works</p><p>(except demolition) a full SWMP must be submitted and approved in writing by the Local</p><p>Planning Authority. The SWMP must detail how in managing any waste arising from</p><p>construction processes, including demolition and groundworks and above ground works, that</p><p>the following targets are met:</p><p>1. Municipal waste recycling rate of 65%</p><p>2. Business waste recycling rate of 75%</p><p>3. Minimum of 95% demolition or site waste diverted from landfill for reuse, recycling or</p><p>recovery</p><p>4. Minimum of 95% of excavation waste diverted from landfill for beneficial use</p><p>5. Minimum of 20% of the new building material elements are comprised of recycled or</p><p>reused content</p><p>REASON: To reduce carbon emissions, enhance climate resilience, promote the circular</p><p>economy, and support low carbon development, in accordance with the London Plan policy</p><p>SI 7, GLA guidance, Local Plan policy LP57 and the NPPF.</p>

<p>Water efficiency</p><p>Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition), a statement to</p><p>confirm that the development has been designed to be water efficient and reduce water</p><p>consumption as far as possible, demonstrating that the development will not exceed a</p><p>maximum water use of 105 litres of water per person per day, with an additional maximum</p><p>water use allowance for external water consumption of 5 litres.</p><p>Strategy, evidence and supporting documentation should be provided and approved in</p><p>writing by the Local Planning Authority pre-commencement showing how water saving</p><p>measures, recycling and water efficiency measures have been incorporated in the design to</p><p>limit both internal and external water use and promote efficient water use.</p><p>REASON: To address the need to conserve water, to mitigate and adapt to climate change,</p><p>taking into account the full range of potential climate change impacts in accordance with the</p><p>London Plan, GLA guidance, Local Plan policy and the NPPF.</p>

<p>AECB Carbonlite</p><p>Prior to first occupation the development hereby approved shall achieve AECB CarbonLite</p><p>certification. The final certificate of completion issued by relevant accredited certifier and</p><p>supporting performance evidence shall be provided to the local authority.</p><p>In the event that the applicant seeks to attain Passivhaus certification, this would be</p><p>welcomed and preferable to AECB Carbonlite, and this enhanced performance certification</p><p>would replace the need for AECB Carbonlite.</p><p>The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details</p><p>thereby approved.</p><p>REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net</p><p>zero development and construction, in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan and</p><p>Section 14 of the National Planning Policy Framework</p>

<p>Low energy buildings</p><p>Prior to first occupation, the applicant must ensure that appropriate guidance is developed by</p><p>a relevant specialist and provided appropriately for residents and occupiers to understand</p><p>how to operate the building’s systems and technologies to maximise sustainable outcomes.</p><p>This should explain:</p><p>A. An explanation of what a Passivhaus building is as compared to typical buildings and low</p><p>energy building is designed to work to provide more sustainable outcomes</p><p>B. An explanation of renewable energy systems and low carbon technologies in place and</p><p>how these should be operated</p><p>C. Troubleshooting and guidance on where any technical issues are encountered and</p><p>provision for feedback on the performance of the building systems in place to ensure the</p><p>building is performing as expected.</p><p>This guidance shall be developed appropriately in a context of other concerns including</p><p>affordability, highlighting any trade-offs that may need to be considered by residents in</p><p>empowering them to adapt use of the building to reduce carbon savings while being</p><p>comfortable.</p><p>This guidance should be developed to be accessible and inclusive, avoiding overly technical</p><p>jargon and considering an appropriate range of needs of likely future residents and</p><p>occupiers. The guidance shall include visual aids, including diagrams and infographics.</p><p>Digital and hard copies should be provided as part of welcome packs and made easily</p><p>accessible on an ongoing basis. The guidance shall be updated at appropriate intervals as</p><p>building management practices and systems change.</p><p>REASON: To support carbon savings reductions in line with Local Plan policy LP55 and</p><p>ensure that renewable energy technologies are adopted for optimal outcomes for residents</p><p>health and wellbeing in line with Local Plan policy LP9, and to support climate resilience for</p><p>Hackney residents in a changing climate in line with Local Plan policy LP54.</p>

<p>Future District Heat Network (DHN) connection</p><p>Prior to the commencement of above ground works (except for demolition) a revised set of</p><p>information demonstrating the ability for future connection to Decentralised Energy Network</p><p>(DEN) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA).</p><p>The submitted details shall include drawings drafted at the appropriate scale and full detailed</p><p>specification of the following, but not be limited to:</p><p>a) Updated evidence of 2 way correspondence between the applicant, the relevant local</p><p>authority and network provider confirming the identified DHN has the capacity to serve the</p><p>development, as well as supporting estimates of the CO2 emission factor to meet the limit set</p><p>out in Part L 2021, installation cost and timescales for connection</p><p>b) Layout of energy centre/plant room showing space for future heat exchanger</p><p>c) Layout of obstacle free safeguarded route between heat exchanger and incoming DEN</p><p>entry point</p><p>d) Details of any on-site connection with pre-installed and capped with flange</p><p>e) Details of any pre-installed pipework connecting identified plant room/ heat exchanger to</p><p>proposed heating system(s)</p><p>Where it has been robustly demonstrated that a refrigerant based heating system (VRF) is</p><p>the only viable option, a retrofit plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA.</p><p>The retrofit plan should:</p><p>1. detail how such system will be upgraded to a wet system compatible with a local DHN</p><p>when there is a viable connection opportunity or when the system reaches its end of</p><p>useful life whichever comes first and</p><p>2. identify who will be responsible to implement the upgrade</p><p>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, the as built drawings and</p><p>specifications demonstrate the ability for future connection to Decentralised Energy Network</p><p>(DEN) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA. The submitted details shall</p><p>include drawings drafted at the appropriate scale and full detailed specification of the</p><p>following, but not be limited to:</p><p>a) as built layout of energy centre/plant room showing space for future heat exchanger</p><p>b) as built layout of obstacle free safeguarded route between heat exchanger and incoming</p><p>DEN entry point</p><p>c) as built details of on-site connection with pre-installed and capped with flange</p><p>d) as built details of pre-installed pipework connecting identified plant room/ heat exchanger</p><p>to proposed heating system(s)</p><p>REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net</p><p>zero development and construction, in accordance with Local Plan policies LP55 and LP56</p><p>and London Plan policies SI2, and SI3 and NPPF section 14.</p>

<p>Healthy materials</p><p>Materials selected for internal finishes and fit out should be low-emitting for Volatile Organic</p><p>Compounds (VOC) or no-VOC. This includes for surface finishes including paints, floorings</p><p>and for kitchen surfacing.</p><p>Materials must not contain hazardous chemicals known to be damaging to human health</p><p>(including toxic heavy metals such as Cadmium and other chemicals/materials including</p><p>creosote, arsenic, CFCs/HCFCs, HFRs, PVC, chlorobenzynes, formaldehyde, lead, mercury</p><p>and phthalates).</p><p>REASON: Due to the airtight environment in Passivhaus buildings the impact of internal</p><p>finishes on human health is of increased relevance. Therefore, internal material selection</p><p>needs to have regard to health and wellbeing of future occupiers alongside securing</p><p>sustainable construction, in accordance with the Local Plan policy LP9.</p>
